lines.text: Do you know how a parachute works? It doesn't stop your fall. It just makes it slow.
When you fall, you have to push the air out of the way. The faster you go, the harder the air pushes back. That push is called drag.
A skydiver stops speeding up at about two hundred kilometres an hour. Drag and weight cancel out.
Open the canopy, and it grabs a huge amount of air. Drag jumps, and the speed drops to around twenty kilometres an hour.
Old round parachutes had a hole in the top, so air could escape and the canopy would not swing.
Modern square parachutes are wings. Air fills the cells, so you can steer, glide, and flare to land softly.
So a parachute is just a way to grab a lot of air, very fast.
